By simulating the population's genetic frequency spectrum, we derive an asymptotic model for a large population using the finite population version of the neutral coalescent. This model is analyzed to determine its convergence and the associated limiting distribution under specific conditions. Furthermore, we propose a non-parametric estimator for the genetic frequency spectrum based on this model, and we investigate its asymptotic and finite-sample properties.

To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive systems and data, speaker verification systems utilize anti-spoofing mechanisms to detect and prevent spoofing attacks. Recent studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of end-to-end approaches in anti-spoofing, yet these models often fail to generalize well for unseen types of spoofing attacks. This paper introduces a novel activation function, the Vigilant activation function, for end-to-end anti-spoofing systems to improve their performance and adaptability. The Vigilant activation function is an adaptive variant of the Leaky Relu function that dynamically regulates the flow of negative information to the output, thus enhancing the model's ability to detect spoofing attacks and perform well in cross-domain scenarios. The proposed method was evaluated on the ASV2019 challenge dataset and achieved outstanding results, surpassing the baseline models in performance and adaptability.

We've developed an effective field theory framework for supergravity with local supersymmetry, applicable to inflationary models. Our approach incorporates a unique method to derive an appropriate supergravity expansion, specifically tailored to the inflationary sector. This framework enables a systematic analysis of effective field theories within supergravity, allowing us to analyze various supergravity expansions up to a certain order and assess their validity.

We investigate the asymmetry in photon pair correlations resulting from three-dimensional momentum interconnections. This asymmetry is quantifiable through a ratio of interconnections and can be experimentally measured by analyzing coincidence counts in a two-dimensional array. This asymmetry is found to be a universal characteristic of momentum-based correlations and is present in cases of random and quasi-crystalline structures. Notably, it serves as a distinct feature that can differentiate momentum-based correlations from other cases.

We have successfully developed a technique for precise terahertz measurements on tiny scales using a superconducting nanowire. This technique enables us to make highly accurate measurements of the complex terahertz permittivity of thin materials in a localized area with a very small focus, achieving a resolution of 100 nm x 100 nm. We have applied this technique to investigate the terahertz properties of thin films and microstrip structures, demonstrating its utility in characterizing planar resonators at terahertz frequencies.

The Borel sets form the most fundamental collection of subsets within the real line, obtained by recursively applying basic operations to the open sets. It has been demonstrated that any partition of the real line into Borel sets necessarily contains a single set that occupies the majority of its extent. Furthermore, if a particular cardinality of Borel sets is present, it must also be the largest cardinality present. This study also shows that any infinite collection of Borel sets, which are all of the same cardinality, must necessarily cover the entire real line.

This study examines the impact of novel investment tactics on established strategies in a dynamic setting. By introducing a novel tactic, existing strategies may become less effective and eventually obsolete. We investigate this phenomenon through agent-based models and find that novel tactics can indeed reduce the effectiveness of established strategies, leading to a decline in their number. However, this outcome is not universal and depends on specific conditions, such as the novel tactic's characteristics and the market environment.

This research explores the feasibility of a new method to identify network protocols in real-time, without requiring explicit packet classification. Our approach relies on fundamental properties of network protocols to create a dynamic system of equations, which can be analyzed using control theory to determine identifiable protocol components. This method has been successfully applied to various open-source tools and extended to detect custom protocols. Furthermore, we have developed several evasion techniques that can mislead this identification method, which we have tested on real-world tools and observed to be effective in some cases.

We investigate the impact of a superconducting strip's proximity effect on a nearby ferromagnetic insulator's spin waves. The superconductor's strip width significantly influences the spin wave's magnetic field's amplitude and extension. Notably, a specific strip width can entirely block the spin wave's magnetic field. This study also examines the effect of the superconductor's strip on a spiral magnetic structure and the spin waves within a ferromagnetic insulator with a 120-degree magnetic structure.

This study explores the challenge of distributed learning for audio classification in the absence of labeled data. We develop a framework allowing a central server to update global models using data from multiple clients, with each client contributing unmarked audio samples from novel classes. The framework incorporates two techniques to ensure accurate representation of novel classes: (i) using unmarked data for gradient estimation via Monte Carlo methods, and (ii) employing novel-sense word embeddings to enhance learning. We evaluate our approach on two distinct audio classification tasks and demonstrate its efficacy in learning models for new classes with limited data.

The creation of high-dimensional entangled states, such as the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state, has significant potential in quantum research, including setting high standards for quantum communication and computation. However, accurately measuring these states in high dimensions is a complex task. This study outlines a comprehensive approach to determine a multi-party high-dimensional GHZ state based on its quantum properties, such as entanglement depth, correlations, and symmetry properties. This proposal can be applied in experiments to accurately identify high-dimensional GHZ states.

This research paper introduces a novel approach to efficient data transmission in large networks by utilizing intelligent reflecting surface technology. To minimize network latency, a rapid channel discovery method is developed for IRS-assisted communication systems. A two-stage protocol is proposed to accelerate the process of gathering channel data from various network devices. A simplified mathematical model is created to optimize the number of messages exchanged within the network. A low-complexity algorithm is derived to determine the optimal message transmission schedule. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage protocol can significantly reduce the number of messages exchanged in the network by up to 90%.

This study examines the relationship between COVID-19 coverage in regional US newspapers, case and death rates, and demographic factors across 210 areas between April and December 2020. It finds a positive correlation between news coverage and COVID-19 metrics in early stages but not in the latter period. Analysis reveals that newspapers in high-incidence areas initially prioritized COVID-19 news more than those in low-incidence areas, and that this shift reversed as the virus spread nationwide. There's a notable disparity in COVID-19 coverage based on demographic factors, particularly in the Northeast where older populations received less coverage despite higher case and death rates.

Research in math education has identified multiple stages in how children learn to count, typically observed in preschool and kindergarten. Building upon this knowledge, we have developed a machine learning framework to simulate these stages by counting a dynamic sequence of sets of objects. The model consists of a series of neural networks, each representing a distinct stage, where the number of objects and their arrangements change between stages. We have successfully trained this model to learn from simple descriptions of object groups and predict correct counts for more complex scenarios.

XOR Filters are a recently developed approximate string matching filter, known to outperform both Bloom and Cuckoo filters in terms of space efficiency and search speed. This study delves into the underlying mechanisms of XOR Filters, comparing them to Bloom Filters in terms of false positive rates and expected filter sizes when dealing with random insertions. It also introduces a simplified variant of the XOR Filter with Chaining algorithm, which offers improved performance and easier implementation.

We have derived equivalences between various classes of convex topological spaces and certain types of complex manifolds, along with associated invariant relationships. Specifically, our research demonstrates that pseudoconvex domains with C0 boundary are equivalent to strictly plurisubharmonic compact K\"ahler manifolds, while pseudoconvex domains with smooth CR-manifolds are equivalent to strictly pseudoconvex compact CR-manifolds. Additionally, our findings show that convex compact K\"ahler manifolds are equivalent to convex compact Hermitian manifolds with positive first Chern class.

A new approach to trend analysis in financial markets is proposed, focusing on the sequential data of trading costs and volumes. This method reveals that past market dynamics are influenced by future events, specifically by the overall trend. It has been mathematically proven that market trends can anticipate their own impact, resulting in a self-fulfilling prophecy. The proposed algorithm is designed to detect and define these trends and is validated through extensive testing on real-time data feeds from various markets, including the US, Europe, and Asia.

Federated learning allows the formation of a shared model through periodic, local model updates from multiple devices, without requiring them to share actual data. This is achieved by gradient updates based on inductive biases, which can be manipulated to influence the learning process. However, existing implementations are vulnerable to manipulation and data leaks. This research presents a robust and privacy-preserving federated learning framework, FLVoogd, to address these issues. Specifically, FLVoogd prevents the exploitation of biased inductive biases and safeguards against data leaks by utilizing secure aggregation techniques. The development of FLVoogd is based on a theoretical analysis of potential vulnerabilities and is demonstrated through the application of a simple classification model, using real-world datasets and a crowd-sourced platform.

Achieving a seamless transition from simulated to real-world environments is a crucial goal in developing autonomous navigation systems. The disparity between these two domains is a significant obstacle known as the Sim2Real gap. In this study, we explore the potential of using image features, specifically gradient information, to bridge the Sim2Real gap for autonomous navigation within indoor spaces. The research focuses on an end-to-end model that maps visual gradients to real-world controls, and we assess its performance by transferring skills learned in a simulated environment to a real-world setting using a mobile robot. The results show that using gradient-based features yields a substantial 30% improvement in performance compared to using RGB features, and we also introduce a novel evaluation metric that prioritizes real-world success.

Significant advancements in deep learning technology have enabled the creation of deepfakes that are increasingly difficult to distinguish from genuine content. This research focuses on the development of countermeasures against deepfake videos that are highly resistant to manipulation. Our study introduces an advanced deepfake detection model, evaluated on various challenging media, including unconstrained video, image, and audio content. The work also explores the application of novel detection algorithms and the integration of existing methods that have shown promise in the field.

Planets in the habitable zone around the Sun are thought to be suitable for life, but their potential for supporting life depends on their internal composition. A new approach is developed to detect and analyze water and volatile compounds within temperate exoplanets by studying their atmospheric transit spectra. This method focuses on the internal structure's impact on atmospheric composition, rather than the reverse. It is based on the equilibrium between water and other compounds in the planet's interior and the thermodynamic balance of atmospheric gases. By comparing the new approach with a traditional model that reversely analyzes atmospheric composition, it is found that the developed method can more accurately identify the presence of a large water reservoir in a planet with a size similar to that of Neptune. Furthermore, it is discovered that the new approach can better distinguish between planets with and without oceans, and it is more sensitive to small amounts of atmospheric hydrogen.

In order to develop spike-based deep neural networks capable of learning from data, we utilize backpropagation through time, modifying it to accommodate spike-based systems. We introduce a leaky-integrate-and-fire model for neurons that incorporates adjustable refractory periods and temporal sampling rates. We also establish a suitable learning rule for spike-based neural networks, one that mimics the efficiency of BPT. We test our approach by training a spiking convolutional neural network on the CIFAR-10 dataset and achieve results comparable to their thresholded activation function-based counterparts.

This report summarizes the findings from the 2022 Out-of-Context Workshop hosted at NAACL, featuring a competition that aimed to assess pre-trained language models in their ability to process text outside of its original context. The participant papers and workshop discussions highlighted the significance of context in language comprehension and the limitations of current language models in handling out-of-context scenarios. The competition itself saw the submission of 17 papers and 4 in-progress papers from 46 authors, with the event receiving support from 5 sponsors.

This study introduces a novel approach for validating generalized polynomial chaos expansions outside their native probabilistic spaces. The method, grounded in the principles of measure theory, enables the comparison of two different approximations of a functional relationship, thereby assessing their accuracy in a systematic manner. The proposed framework is demonstrated in two case studies, including one that analyzes the dynamics of a particle under a strong gravitational force and another that studies a differential equation with a non-self-adjoint operator.

In various industries such as healthcare and the Internet of Things, large systems consist of interconnected components where some sensors may not receive data and others may provide inaccurate readings due to failures. This paper presents a new approach to identify and isolate changes in such systems in real-time using real data. Our method can handle a wide range of dynamic systems where some sensors have incomplete data and others may have failed. It can also detect changes in real-time and isolate problematic sensors without affecting the system's overall performance. This approach is based on a new model that combines the principles of the Hotelling T-squared statistic and the multivariate cumulative distribution function. It can be applied to systems with a small number of sensors and variables, making it suitable for use in small embedded devices. This paper also presents a new method to estimate the performance of this approach and compares it with existing methods using real data from a healthcare setting.

We've conducted a comprehensive analysis of 54 dwarf galaxies from the SDSS-DR16 using their chemical compositions and star evolution histories. Our research reveals distinct chemical characteristics linked to each dwarf galaxy type, with the abundance of alpha-elements and metallicity showing the most notable variations. Notably, dwarf galaxies with high satellite fractions tend to have elevated alpha-element abundances and lower metal content compared to those with low satellite fractions. Our findings also indicate that the abundance of iron and nickel is significantly higher in dwarf galaxies with high satellite fractions, whereas the abundance of silicon and sulfur is higher in those with low satellite fractions. Our research further shows that the star formation history of these galaxies is intricately connected to their chemical compositions, with the star formation history influenced by the abundance of alpha-elements and metal content.

We introduce a spectrum $N\Gamma$ derived from the homotopy action of a profinite group $\Gamma$ on a sequence of spaces $\{X_n\}_{n\ge 0}$, which serves as a powerful tool to investigate the homotopy orbit spectra $X_n\wedge_{\mathbb{Z}}\Gamma$ and perfect group analogues. Our approach provides a unified framework to study these cases, offering novel applications and simplifying existing methods.

Document analysis models that focus on visual details require a large number of labeled examples, which can be costly to obtain.  To reduce the expense of labeling, we investigate the effectiveness of using inexpensive text-based labels for tasks that require image data.  Our approach uses text-based labels to pre-train a linear model, which is then fine-tuned with limited labeled data.  We demonstrate the feasibility of using inexpensive text-based labels for tasks like OCR, image captioning, and table extraction, outperforming models with no pre-training or models with expensive image-based labels.

The EuS/InAs interface is a crucial component in numerous spin-orbit-coupled systems and has been extensively studied. However, the electronic properties of this interface are still not fully understood, particularly when it comes to the influence of different bonding arrangements between Eu and InAs atoms. Using a combination of first-principles calculations and many-body theory, we have investigated the electronic properties of the EuS/InAs interface and how they vary depending on the bonding configuration. Our results show that the electronic states at the interface are significantly influenced by the bonding arrangement, resulting in either p-type or n-type behavior. Additionally, we have identified two possible charge transfer mechanisms and have analyzed the impact of different bonding configurations on the magnetic properties at the interface.

We provide an efficient classification of Borel Wadge classes by introducing a novel system of transfinite games, $<_{\alpha}$, for $\alpha<2^{\aleph_0}$, which builds upon Sargent's game $<_S$. We demonstrate that the Borel Wadge degrees form a complete lattice under the Borel Wadge relation and can be described as the closed set of a topological space. Furthermore, we establish an isomorphism between the semi-lattice of open sets and the collection of games $<_{\alpha}$ for countable $\alpha$. This discovery enables a simplified classification of Borel Wadge classes by analyzing the structure of games $<_{\alpha}$.

Deepening convolutional neural networks is often hindered by their growing size due to increased depth. ClickTrain is an efficient pruning method that allows networks to be trained in their full depth without the usual scaling limitations. This method is based on a local pattern and can be applied to a wide range of networks without needing any further modifications. Experiments show that ClickTrain achieves precise results, with only a minimal impact on accuracy, and scales well, with a linear increase in resources for larger networks.

This research expands the Distributive Complete Lambek Calculus with modal operators, as previously defined by Alves and Brogi, by introducing a more comprehensive system that includes modal functions. We resolve the issue of SLD-resolution refutability in the enhanced calculus, and demonstrate that its clausal provability is decidable.

The detection of gravitational waves from merging compact objects marks a significant breakthrough in multi-messenger astronomy. Future gravitational wave detectors will likely identify tens of thousands of events per year from neutron star-black hole mergers, allowing us to study the detailed physical processes of these collisions. We employed deep learning models to identify and categorize neutron star-black hole merger simulations, analyzing various combinations of neutron star and black hole properties. Our results indicate that a convolutional neural network can accurately distinguish between different neutron star masses using only gravitational wave data, and that a custom-designed architecture is necessary to effectively classify various neutron star masses.

A new study has identified a transiting exoplanet, TOI-5542.05, orbiting the star TOI-5542 every 9.97 days. This planet has a radius similar to that of Jupiter and a mass estimated to be around 1.23 Jupiter masses. TOI-5542 is a G9-type star with a low metallicity, which is unusual given that planets with this characteristic typically have higher metallicities. TOI-5542.05 is likely an old planet, given its large size and the properties of the host star. This planet is expected to be a hot Jupiter, which formed far from its star and migrated inward. TOI-5542.05 is one of the smallest hot Jupiters discovered to date.

Constrained Markov Choice Models (CMMC) extend upon existing preference learning techniques by incorporating a set of non-parametric constraints that help to eliminate spurious alternatives from a learner's preferences. This research presents a new and efficient algorithm to learn CMMC parameters, which operates within a primal-dual framework. This method is based on a dynamic programming approach to update a dual variable, maintaining duality gap reduction and ensuring model constraints compliance. The study also establishes the asymptotic consistency of the CMMC parameters and preference rankings. The algorithm's performance is further demonstrated through simulations on real-world data.

A unique application of Offline Handwritten Mathematical Notation Recognition (HMNIR) is the ability to recognize handwritten math from paper, a crucial feature for math teaching and learning. Although online math recognition has been extensively researched, offline HMNIR has received less attention. In this paper, we present a comprehensive system for offline HMNIR, utilizing a complex math dataset called Math-101D. The system comprises two key components: a handwritten math-specific dataset and a deep learning-based framework. The dataset, Math-101D, is an extension of the original Math-101 dataset, which was created by adding a difficult stroke type to the original strokes. The system's framework is designed to address the complexities of handwritten math by breaking it down into three sub-tasks: stroke recognition, symbol recognition, and layout recognition. The framework utilizes a combination of convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks, along with a graph-based approach, to achieve these sub-tasks. The results of our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with the system achieving a high overall accuracy of 92.6% on the Math-101D dataset.

We investigate a supersymmetric quantum mechanics related to a hermitian vector bundle on a complex manifold, expanding sheaf cohomology. Our analysis reveals that supersymmetric ground states are closely tied to nontrivial cohomology classes in both finite and infinite dimensions. This connection enables us to establish a general framework for calculating quantum mechanics outcomes through sheaf cohomology. Furthermore, our findings can be applied to a broad range of mathematical frameworks, including both classical algebraic geometry and a quantum version with noncommutative geometry characteristics.

The study of complex networks has been a prominent area of research, with various theories and models developed to analyze their behavior and properties. This work builds on previous studies by examining the variability of network systems that change over time, using a complex system of interacting agents represented as a complex network. A measure of variability is introduced to analyze and compare different network configurations, and it is found that a network's stability and resilience can be improved through specific types of connections. These findings are applicable to a range of complex network models, including those based on percolation and percolation with percolation transition.

Actor-critic methods have achieved significant success in a range of reinforcement learning tasks. However, they often face the challenge of exploring action spaces effectively, particularly in tasks with multiple degrees of freedom. This research investigates the potential of combining these methods with the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) technique to improve exploration. HMC leverages gradient information to propel the actor towards promising regions of its distribution. We demonstrate the efficacy of this combination in a multi-armed bandit task and two scenarios with multiple degrees of freedom: controlling a quadruped robot and a task involving a 7-DoF robotic arm.

A fundamental concept in Number Theory is the Twin Prime Conjecture, which posits the existence of an infinite number of pairs of prime numbers that differ by 2. The proof presented here is inspired by Euclid's infinite prime numbers proof and is adapted for two variable functions to show the infinite number of prime pairs under a specific condition.

Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) rely on sonar technology to create detailed maps of their surroundings, enabling them to operate in unfamiliar environments and adapt to changing conditions. However, the use of multiple sonars with different fields of view can lead to inconsistencies in the generated maps, making it necessary to combine their data in real-time to ensure accurate navigation. This paper presents a method for immediately sonar data fusion using a layered manager, which takes into account the unique characteristics of each sonar and adapts to the vehicles' movement in three dimensions. The proposed approach is demonstrated to be effective in real-world scenarios, outperforming existing sonar data fusion methods.

We've analyzed the near-infrared reflectance spectrum of Nereid, a satellite of Neptune, which orbits within the 5.6 micrometer Methane absorption band. This analysis suggests that Nereid's surface consists of two parts: one with a mixture of water ice and dark organic material, and another with pure water ice. The ratio of these two components can be adjusted to fit different observations. The model also indicates that Nereid's spectrum can be matched using a mixture of ices found in comets, which implies that Nereid's composition is similar to that of comets.

We examine affine and projective surfaces defined by specific 3x3 matrices with lower triangular entries in the ring of lower triangular matrices with integer entries, and investigate their geometric properties. We establish that these surfaces are related to projective lines in a non-degenerate way, and demonstrate that some of these surfaces are minimal, while others are not. We also show that these surfaces are neither rational nor of maximal singularity degree.

We introduce a Tukey-sequence with regard to almost-everywhere equality in measure, predicated on a modified version of the first part of Pawlikowski's theorem from 1986. Furthermore, our work generalizes the second part of Pawlikowski's theorem to a setting involving a broader range of cardinalities.

In the context of a dynamic treatment regime, pessimism serves as a conservative strategy to ensure offline policy evaluation remains unbiased, even when the model is slightly inaccurate. This pessimism is typically achieved through a conservative offline policy, often assumed to be the "no treatment" approach. However, in scenarios where this assumption is not valid, we propose an alternative conservative offline policy based on Bayesian learning. This new approach can be illustrated by modifying the Thompson sampler, which yields a conservative policy that maintains unbiased offline policy evaluation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in a simulation study and provide a real-world example to showcase its applicability.

This note explores the relationship between local duality for principal ideal domains in the context of local cohomology modules, drawing inspiration from a broader theorem by Roberts and Thrall. It also examines the applications of this relationship in the contexts of Frobenius functors and Hilbert functions.

We introduce a proposal for a 26-qubit lattice system, derived from a reformulated $E_8$ graph by incorporating additional vertices and edges to explore the connections between a quantum system's entanglement and the constraints imposed by the Grothendieck's inequality in quantum contextuality. The 26-qubit setup enables us to examine the boundaries of maximal entanglement and the Grothendieck's limit, thereby serving as a valuable tool to experimentally investigate the relationship between entanglement and contextuality.

We investigate the occurrence of superconductivity in a three-component system consisting of two repulsive fermions and one attractive fermion, which interacts within a topological flat band. Our findings demonstrate that under specific conditions, a general superconducting state can emerge, comprising various combinations of pairings. Additionally, we establish that the phase boundaries of superconducting pairings are influenced by the relative strengths of the interactions between particles. Our analysis further reveals that superconductivity can be stabilized over a wider range of interactions when the attractive interaction preferentially affects one spin component, rather than acting equally on all components.

The original Universal Polya's theorem was first formulated by George Polya in 1923 for the group of integers, describing how the number of divisors of any positive integer $n$ grows as a function of the prime number $t$ representing the upper limit of the prime factorization of $n$. In this article, we adapt and generalize Polya's theorem for the group of functions from one-dimensional finite simplicial complexes to the nonnegative integers, based on the number of divisors in the corresponding polynomial of degree one that represents the complex.

In presence-absence data, each sample is represented by a count of species, typically denoted as $N(0,\sigma^2)$. This format is commonly used in ecological studies, differing from standard multivariate data which are represented as $N(\mu,\sigma^2)$. Clustering presence-absence data poses unique challenges, particularly in high dimensions with a large number of species. Our research evaluates the effectiveness of multiple clustering methods for presence-absence data, including those based on multivariate statistical models, information theory, and network analysis. We examine the performance of these methods in simulated data and show that they produce comparable results.

This paper presents a unified framework for salient object detection using RGB and RGB-D images. The proposed method integrates two sub-networks: a feature extraction module and a cross-modal fusion sub-network. The cross-modal fusion sub-network fuses RGB and depth information Fusing RGB and depth information enables the framework to capture both visual and geometric characteristics of salient objects. The framework's novelty lies in its two-stage training process, allowing for the effective learning of RGB and depth extraction modules. The proposed method outperforms existing techniques in salient object detection, according to the results of experiments conducted on the AECOM dataset and the recently released NUS-16F dataset.

This paper details our systems for two subtasks of SemEval-2019 Task 6.  We developed models for both subtasks A and B using BERT and Support Vector Machines.  Our BERT-based model for subtask A leveraged a pre-trained BERT model and fine-tuned it with a dataset from Twitter, achieving a macro F1 score of 0.44 in the official evaluation.  For subtask B, our model combined the predictions of an SVM classifier trained on BERT word embeddings and a BERT-based classifier.  In the official evaluation, this multi-strategy approach yielded a macro F1 score of 0.34.

We examine the quotients of two infinite sequences, symmetrical numbers and antisymmetrical numbers, which are generated by the recurrence relations $a_{n+1}=a_n+na_{n-1}$ and $b_{n+1}=-b_n+na_{n-1}$. We find that the quotients of these sequences, resulting from successively dividing lower terms by higher terms, converge to a constant value of $\sqrt{2}$, regardless of whether we start with symmetrical or antisymmetrical sequences.

This study introduces a non-convex variational framework for a multi-faceted inverse problem in computed tomography (CT) imaging. The problem involves reconstructing a CT image from a single scan using a polyenergetic X-ray source, while accounting for energy-dependent attenuation and using a CT scanner with multiple photon-counting detectors. The proposed framework treats these factors in a unified mathematical model and demonstrates its effectiveness through numerical simulations.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) in developing countries is a complex task due to limited resources, noisy images, and multiple languages being written in a single script. While datasets like IAM and GTSDB provide some assistance, they don't fully address the issue of script and language variability. To overcome this limitation, we've developed a new approach that can learn from a small amount of labeled data and automatically create new, diverse handwritten text examples. Our method can handle a wide range of languages in different scripts and can adapt to new conditions without retraining. We've tested it on IAM and GTSDB datasets with positive results.

A combined approach using ab initio methods has been taken to study heavy nuclei. Specifically, the lightest nucleons in the nucleus are described using a Monte Carlo method known as the iMCDG2n+U deformed Hartree-Fock method, while a variational approach is applied to the heaviest nucleons. The effective interaction used is derived from chiral perturbation theory, with the 3-body forces computed using an in-medium effective framework. The computational method has been successfully applied to the rotational bands of even-even nuclei, yielding accurate results that match experimental data and predictions from other theoretical models.

This work delves into the core ideas underlying topological quantum phenomena, illustrated through the one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Hubbard model. By dissecting the model's topological properties in both static and dynamic contexts, we demonstrate how various notions of topological concepts, such as the entanglement spectrum, entanglement entropy, and Chern numbers, are interconnected. Our analysis reveals that these concepts converge in the free fermion scenario but exhibit a divergence in the interacting fermion case, where the dynamics of entanglement entropy fails to capture the model's topological characteristics.

This study demonstrates the compactness of the composition map $F \mapsto F \circ \phi$ within specific Bergman space contexts, where $\phi$ is a biholomorphic mapping of a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ to another. If $\phi$ is closely related to a disk mapping $\psi$, the result is a characterization of compactness involving the Littlewood-Paley function applied to $F \circ \psi$.

We have developed a dual supergravity model in AdS$_5$ space coupled with a self-dual gauge field, which accurately represents the low-energy, long-wavelength aspects of Type IIB string theory on a specific curved surface. By applying a coordinate transformation, we demonstrate the equivalence of our model to a previously established dual supergravity model, thereby extending its scope to include spacetimes with both de Sitter and flat boundaries. We have also derived the corresponding effective supercurrents in the associated CFT using AdS/CFT correspondence.

This paper introduces DynaSOAr, a high-performance, concurrent memory allocator designed for object-oriented programming on GPUs. By leveraging the CPU's cache hierarchy during host memory allocation, DynaSOAr enhances memory usage efficiency on GPUs by grouping contiguous device memory. The experimental results demonstrate that DynaSOAr outperforms current GPU memory allocators by 1.27 times to 1.53 times, depending on the specific benchmark.

We investigate a $U(1)_X$ model based on the gauge group $SU(2)_L \otimes SU(2)_R \otimes SU(2)_I \otimes U(1)_X \otimes U(1)_Y$ where the $U(1)_X$ and $U(1)_Y$ charges are linked to baryon and dark matter sectors. The $U(1)_X$ charge assignments are inspired by two different high-energy theories: $SO(10)$ and $E_6$. In the first scenario, the $U(1)_X$ charge is directly derived from three complete $SU(5)$ representations of $B-L$ charges, while in the second, it is derived from two sets of $E_6$ charges. We then examine the baryon sector's behavior under two different $U(1)_X$ charge assignment methods and identify the Lagrangian terms that violate baryon number conservation. We also explore the dark matter mass and decay rate, as well as the dark matter-proton cross-section, and calculate the LHC constraints on the model.

Researchers investigated the impact of internal pressures on a cylindrical pipe made of a composite material, consisting of a hollow core surrounded by a layer of a thermoplastic polymer and an outer wrapping of a glass fiber-reinforced polymer. The material's properties were first examined, followed by a finite element analysis to simulate the internal pressure's effects. The results showed that the stress on the hollow core exceeded its strength under a specified internal pressure of 10 bar, indicating a loss of mechanical integrity. To assess the consequences of this failure, researchers conducted a series of tests, including a simulation of the pipe's sudden rupture, which revealed that the pressure drop following a failure would not be sufficient to prevent the entry of hazardous materials.

This paper presents a method to ensure robustness in Bayesian network classification when there's uncertainty about the network structure. It allows for the calculation of a reliable classification boundary by finding the least probable level of classification error on a probabilistic circuit. We demonstrate that this approach can be applied to linear and polynomial probabilistic circuits, providing a way to estimate the highest probability level of classification error within a certain margin of uncertainty.

In a superfluid, a quantum impurity subjected to an oscillating potential experiences a prolonged, slow motion along the direction of the oscillations, lasting longer than its equivalent in regular Bose-Einstein condensates. This phenomenon, referred to as a prolonged Bloch oscillation, is observed in two types of superfluid Bose-Einstein condensates: those with and without a roton minimum in their dispersion relation. A theoretical model has demonstrated that the prolonged slowing down of the impurity's oscillations in superfluids is a direct result of the formation of a bound state between the impurity and a quasiparticle excitation. This bound state is a signature of the prolonged slowing down, and its characteristics are discussed in detail.

A code is considered neighbor-transitive if it remains invariant under the graph's neighborhood operator. This property is shared by codes that are highly dispersed in certain graphs. The study explores the relationship between neighbor-transitive codes and partial dispersions within the context of generalized quadrangles. The paper establishes a complete classification of neighbor-transitive codes in classical generalized quadrangles and presents a partial outcome for the Berger and classical generalized quadrangles.

The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) within the Milky Way's center exhibits a complex, anisotropic mass distribution pattern. To quantify this anisotropy, we employed a two-dimensional cross-correlation function in a study using the Herschel Gould Belt Survey data. By analyzing the mass configuration of the CMZ, we found that its spatial pattern is significantly influenced by anisotropic mass distribution at a scale of approximately 20 parsecs. Our findings indicate that the mass distribution in the CMZ is more concentrated along the east-west axis, with a peak at around 10 degrees east of north. This discovery supports previous research suggesting that the CMZ is shaped by torques resulting from a bar-like structure in the Milky Way's bulge.

A rate equation model is developed to analyze the time-dependent changes in X-ray Absorption Near Edge Spectroscopy (XANES) transmission signals at high fluence levels. This model is specifically designed for third-row transition metal and transition metal doped systems, taking into account the creation and annihilation of electrons based on specific energy excitations and relaxations. It is demonstrated that the model is capable of accurately reproducing the experimentally observed delayed transmission increases in L-edge XANES experiments conducted on 4d-4f transition metal ions.

A temperature sensing circuit utilizing a subthreshold CMOS inverter with reduced power consumption has been designed to operate within a wide temperature range. The design incorporates a temperature-to-voltage converter and a digital counter to produce a binary output, enabling temperature measurement with a 0.24 degrees Celsius resolution and approximately one degree Celsius error margin. The integrated circuit was fabricated using a 0.13$\mu$m CMOS technology process and demonstrated an energy efficiency of 1.06 nanojoules per conversion, with a 3.71 megahertz conversion rate and 1.2 milliwatts power consumption.

Heralded entanglement swapping without the need for post-selection is a crucial technique for generating entangled photons on a large scale. This method, however, is often limited by the post-selection process itself, especially when dealing with polarization entanglement. This study introduces a new approach, leveraging quantum scissors to create polarization entanglement in a single step. By utilizing a quantum scissor metamaterial, we demonstrate the simultaneous generation of two entangled photons with orthogonal polarizations, achieving a high entanglement fidelity of 0.983 and a high single-photon visibility of 0.983 as well.

We investigate the creation of virtual Euclidean spanners in metric spaces. A virtual Euclidean spanner is a geometric structure that allows the calculation of approximate distances to within a specified factor, while also enabling the determination of true distances between any two points at a cost not exceeding a predetermined ratio. We present efficient algorithms for constructing such spanners with optimal distortion values in certain types of metric spaces, as well as for general Euclidean spaces with a specified scale. Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of lower bounds on the distortion values achievable by such spanners in certain types of metric spaces, as well as in the geometric t-spaces metric.

The proliferation of IoT devices has led to an abundance of data, but extracting relevant features from this data is a complex and resource-intensive task, especially when faced with a multitude of features. This makes it crucial to employ an efficient feature selection method that balances performance and computational costs. This work proposes an innovative, cost-aware feature extraction technique that efficiently selects features based on an entropy-based strategy, thereby reducing the dimensionality of the data and a subsequent classifier. The method's performance and efficiency were evaluated on real-world IoT data from UbiFlow, showcasing its potential to be a valuable tool in IoT data analysis.

Godel modal logic encompasses a family of modal logics characterized by the (4) axiom, which can be modelled through Godel algebras with a (4)-compatible lattice order. This paper expands on this framework by investigating relational structures that can serve as semantic models for Godel modal logic and its (K) 4-dualistic extensions. It introduces specific types of Godel algebras with a lattice order, incorporating the (4) and (K) 4-dualistic axioms, and demonstrates the correspondence between these algebras and certain classes of relational structures. Furthermore, the paper identifies specific types of Godel algebras with a lattice order that correspond to prelinicity and double Godelity in modal logic.

This paper presents a method for creating word alignments in sign languages by leveraging bilingual corpora from spoken languages. The sign language community faces a significant challenge in accessing bilingual corpora due to the limited availability of native speakers. To overcome this issue, we propose utilizing existing bilingual corpora from spoken languages and adapting them to sign languages through machine learning models that capture the grammatical structure of sign languages. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by creating word alignments for two sign languages, Danish and Swedish, based on a corpus of Danish and Swedish conversations.

We introduce a distorted resolvent method to find Nash equilibria for a broad class of nonsmooth games through monotone variational inequalities. This method enables us to analyze Nash equilibria in various applications, including nonsmooth optimization, differential inclusions with constraints, and both finite and infinite pure Nash games.

Primordial Black Holes are considered as a potential candidate for dark matter, with some variants having the potential to act as dark energy due to their gravitational effects on the universe's large-scale structure. The PopSyCLE code is used to simulate the universe's evolution, incorporating various models of Primordial Black Holes as dark energy. The code's accuracy is validated through a comparison of its matter and radiation density predictions with established cosmological values. The study examines the impact of different PopSyCLE parameters on the simulated matter power spectrum and finds that models with early-peaking PBH densities are more favorable. The research also investigates the potential of PBH models to explain the observed tension between galaxy distributions and the cosmic microwave background, with some models indicating a possible resolution of this discrepancy.

In a system consisting of balls arranged in a two-dimensional space with periodic boundary conditions, we simulate the development of complex patterns as a result of their collision. The rules governing these collisions lead to the formation of patterns characterized by a non-traditional type of ordering, one that is dynamically modulated in a non-repeating manner. The existence of different stages, each exhibiting a unique form of ordering, is observed, and we find that the transition between these stages depends on the system's size and a specific parameter, known as the collision module. The patterns that emerge in this system are found to be similar to those seen in certain liquid crystal colloids under shear, where a specific type of ordering is modulated in a non-repeating pattern.

This study introduces novel linear discrete-time recurrences for solving the steady-state spatial mean square error of two Gaussian random fields on the sphere, one of which is known and the other unknown. We provide two recurrences, each applicable in different scenarios, requiring only the current and previous values of the field's state vector. These recurrences significantly simplify the solution of this steady-state mean square error problem, allowing for the use of standard numerical methods to solve the resulting algebraic Riccati equation.

We suggest a concept for visualizing quantum states using single photons, without the need for continuous measurement. Our approach leverages the undetected photon phenomenon, enabling the creation of an effective single-pixel Fock space for visualizing quantum states. We demonstrate the ability to accurately visualize Fock states and continuous variable states, achieving notable results with undetected photons.

The interaction between liquid liquid interfaces is a long-standing interest in scientific study. When two liquid drops are placed on a soap foam, causing it to get stuck due to surface tension, leading to an increase in the foam's friction. This effect is primarily caused by the increase in the foam's viscosity, which is a result of the creation of a complex liquid network at the drop-drop interface. The frictional force is proportional to the size of the drops and the surface tension of the liquid, while it is independent of the drops' weight. The increase in frictional force is also influenced by the type of liquid used, as well as the presence of surfactants.

Cutaneous carcinoma identification is a complex task due to the diversity of skin diseases and the need to distinguish them from common benign skin conditions. The INRIA dataset, which includes a wide range of skin lesions, is often used to evaluate algorithms for carcinoma identification. However, the dataset lacks carcinoma samples, and the task is framed as a multi-class problem to increase its complexity. The identification of outliers within the INRIA dataset is crucial to exclude irrelevant data points and improve model performance. A deep learning model is proposed, which incorporates entropy into the loss function to identify and eliminate anomalous data during training. The model is then evaluated on the INRIA dataset, and experiments are conducted to determine the effectiveness of the proposed method.

We have calculated the lifetime of quasi-particles in sodium using ab initio many-body calculations. The calculations took into account the influence of long-range electron-electron interactions but also constrained the strong coupling limit. The results revealed that the lifetime of quasi-particles in sodium is on the order of 10^-14 seconds, which is comparable to experimental findings. The study also showed that the leading cause of quasi-particle decay is related to the velocity dispersion of electrons rather than their density.

Microstate dynamics is analyzed using phase space trajectories, which can be studied with or without knowledge of their initial conditions. This study introduces a method to track non-repeating trajectories in closed systems over time, highlighting their diverse paths in the phase space. A specific technique is developed to identify unique Hamiltonian paths, which helps resolve issues related to the variation in phase space volume and the origin problem in thermodynamics. A key application of this approach is the examination of the free expansion of a microcanonical or canonical ideal gas. Results show that, contrary to common beliefs, there is no single "correct" trajectory representing a free expansion, and instead, there are an infinite number of Hamiltonian paths with distinct characteristics.

This passage examines the local expansion of a graph-based formula for a 2-tensor field's pushforward under a diffeomorphism in two dimensions. The examined formula is an element of a broader graph-based approach for calculating symplectic structures and their pushforwards on 2-manifolds. A key component of this approach involves weights, which are complex calculations used to define the structure. The passage demonstrates that these weights can be expressed as finite sums of combinatorial terms, which are in turn defined by the geometry of the graph. A specific type of graph, known as a curvature graph, is used to extend the formula beyond diffeomorphisms to other 2-tensor fields. The weights used in this extension are referred to as curvature weights. The passage shows that curvature weights can also be expressed as finite sums of combinatorial terms.

We investigate the dynamics of a single particle moving through a weakly nonlinear woodpile chain and a diatomic granular chain. The phase diagram for both systems is examined, which shows how the presence of nonlinearity affects the rotation period of the particle. The phase diagram is found to have three distinct regions, where the particle's motion changes from localized to extended and then becomes rotational. The influence of nonlinearity is most pronounced in the localized regime, where it causes the particle's rotation period to decrease. In the three-humped regime, nonlinearity has a minimal effect on the particle's rotation period, which instead depends on its mass relative to the surrounding grains. In contrast, the rotational regime is not significantly affected by nonlinearity, where the particle's rotation period is instead determined by its mass relative to the surrounding grains.

In the early universe, a primordial abundance of heavy fields could give rise to a cosmic version of particle collider physics, where the cosmological landscape's inherent fluctuations serve as a natural "smuggling" mechanism, bypassing the light-speed barrier to create observable signatures in the Large Scale Structure. These cosmic signatures can be extracted using a non-linear bias analysis, revealing a primal feature characteristic of the primordial spectrum, which is a distinct, oscillating pattern within the nearly scale-invariant power law. This primal feature is a universal indicator of heavy field Standard CMB models and can be identified through LSS data, even in the presence of primordial non-Gaussianity.

A graph structure called the accordion chart is defined and its properties are explored, establishing its Hamiltonian nature and perfect matching characteristics. Additionally, a characterization of accordion charts is derived as quartic circulant graphs, which reveals a novel representation for these graphs, offering a potential utility in graph coloring studies.

We examine a three-state quantum walk system where one of the states is constantly ignored and focus on its dynamics. Ignoring a state is equivalent to a specific quantum state collapse after each step, resulting from the system's Hamiltonian being ill-conditioned. We derive an equation that governs the global spread of the wave packet, based on the condition number of the underlying graph's Laplacian. This equation is applicable to a broad range of quantum walk models and we verify its accuracy through numerical simulations.

In the realm of computer vision, pre-trained models have become the preferred choice for downstream tasks due to their ability to capture universal features. Recent advancements in Vision Transformers (ViTs) have made them a suitable alternative to Convolutional Neural Networks. This research focuses on the Self-Guided Vision Transformer (SGViT), an improvement over existing ViTs that enhances their performance in downstream tasks. By introducing a multi-head self-attention block with a dynamic weighting scheme based on input values, SGViT allows ViTs to effectively capture both low and high-level features. The theoretical underpinnings of SGViT's design are supported by analysis of its attention patterns and the model's training efficiency. The efficacy of SGViT is demonstrated through experiments on various downstream tasks, including image classification, segmentation, object detection, and image restoration, showcasing its ability to develop desirable properties and achieve superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models.

In this research, we have developed a six-dimensional dissipative dark energy model, referred to as dissipative combined dark fluid model, by combining the dark matter and dark energy into a single entity called the dark fluid. The model's equations were derived using the Dicke's power law variation cosmological principle and solved analytically. A graphical representation of the phase space is provided to examine the dissipative and irreversible processes occurring in the model. Furthermore, we have investigated the cosmological parameters, such as the deceleration parameter, Hubble parameter, and the equation of state parameters, and analyzed their behavior in relation to the dissipative and irreversible processes.

We present a simple proof that the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations has a critical issue in terms of stability, specifically using Sobolev spaces with high smoothness and certain types of Lorentz spaces with smoothness.

In the realm of text-to-image generation, the steady introduction of semantic guidance in the latent space of diffusion models has been found to significantly enhance image quality. However, the optimal approach for incorporating semantic information remains unclear, particularly when it comes to the order and frequency of semantic interventions throughout the creation process. This study investigates the impact of different semantic creation strategies on the image quality produced by diffusion models, using a range of creator architectures and semantic providers. The findings reveal that a systematic, continuous injection of semantic information leads to the creation of high-quality images with improved semantic fidelity.

This research introduces a novel method for concealing image data by modifying pixels in an invertible manner. A specific type of neural network, called a Bayesian Neural Network, is utilized to create an invertible function that can be applied to pixel values, resulting in a predictable shift. Subsequently, an image filtering technique is employed to create an effective masking method that can be reversed by utilizing the network's parameters as additional input data. This approach is demonstrated to provide a strong steganographic method that can withstand various statistical analysis attacks.

The $J/\psi$ leptonically decaying into a photon pair and a neutrino or dark energy particle is examined. The invisible decay products are assumed to be a lepton pair separated by a large distance, forming a cone with a minimal angle. The study focuses on the observable, invisible, and off-shell components of the invisible decay width. The results show that the dark energy invisible decay width is sensitive to the neutrino mass and dark energy equation of state parameters. The dark energy invisible decay width is more sensitive to the neutrino mass when the dark energy parameter is close to -1, but when it's close to 0, it's more sensitive to the parameter itself. The neutrino invisible decay width is more sensitive to the neutrino mass when the parameter is greater than 0.5. The study also shows that the standard model predictions for the $J/\psi$ invisible decay width are consistent with experimental data.

The study of solar activity is crucial to understanding high-energy events that can impact Earth. To analyze solar flares, researchers focus on small, bright magnetic features that appear on the solar surface. These features are typically described using a one-part Gaussian distribution, but this approach is insufficient for larger, more active structures that require a two-part Gaussian model to accurately represent their behavior. This study examines data from the SDO and HMI instruments and shows that these features follow a two-part Gaussian model, similar to previous studies on smaller, less active structures. The results indicate that both types of features share similar characteristics, but with a difference in proportions, and that the combination of these features, along with their characteristics, is necessary to fully understand solar activity.

Human vision can quickly identify and break down complex scenes into basic components, known as minimal clips. Researchers have created computational models to replicate this ability, but the efficiency and speed of these models are limited compared to human vision. This study investigates whether these models can learn from real-world data, specifically by training them on human-created minimal clips. The results show that while these models can learn to identify objects and movements, they struggle to identify high-level actions and interactions, such as pouring a liquid from a bottle. The study also identifies key challenges in developing dynamic object recognition models, including dealing with occlusions, object movement, and variations in object appearance.

This research explores the possibility that microscopic magnetic monopoles, referred to as "shadow monopoles," are responsible for the weakening of large-scale magnetic fields in the universe. We propose that these shadow monopoles have extremely low masses, on the order of picograms or femtograms, and are electrically charged as well. We find that the interaction between these shadow monopoles and cosmic rays could effectively break the symmetry of magnetic fields in galaxies and galaxy clusters, thereby explaining their observed weakening. Furthermore, we suggest that the same process could be responsible for the overall decrease in strength of magnetic fields throughout the universe's evolution.

Climate forecasting is a critical issue that has significant implications for both climate modeling and adaptation. Advances in deep learning have led to the development of various climate forecasting models, but they often face challenges such as high dimensionality, data sparsity, and non-stationary climate patterns. In this work, we introduce a new transformer-based model that combines shifted window cross-attention with a novel spatial attention mechanism. By leveraging the self-parallelism of the transformer architecture, our method efficiently handles the complexity of spatio-temporal climate data. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on the climate time series forecasting task, where it achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models.

In this study, we investigate the possibility of using the $S_3$-symmetric three-Higgs-doublet model to explain both dark matter and recent observations of CP-violation in neutrinos. We present two different approaches, one where the dark matter sector interacts with the neutrino sector via a portal, and another where the dark matter is composed of a ghost field, which is stabilized by a $C$-odd ghost field. In both scenarios, we determine the model parameters that are consistent with theoretical requirements and dark matter stability, before analyzing the model's scalar sector using a numerical approach. In the portal interaction scenario, we find that the model can accommodate large neutrino CP phases, while also satisfying dark matter stability and theoretical constraints. In the ghost-based scenario, we find that the model parameters are heavily restricted, but we identify a range of values that meet the theoretical requirements and demonstrate a potential connection to recent studies on dark matter interactions.

The PPTQ hypothesis, a key concept in quantum computation, states that all quadrilateral convex operators are completely positive, which we demonstrate to be false with counterexamples. However, we do find that all PPT quadrilaterals are indeed completely positive, upholding a related conjecture.

In neurons, substances like neurotransmitters and hormones are transported from the synapse to the cell body along transport routes with limited capacity and regulated speed. This process is crucial for substance reception, but can be impaired due to congestion, affecting the substances' journey and ultimately their availability. We developed a mathematical model that uses an optimization technique to simulate substance transport and adjust route speeds for clogs, given varying substance influxes and unique properties for each transport route. Our model's performance is demonstrated by its alignment with a partial differential equation system, which represents a more intricate, yet computationally complex aspect of substance transport.

In the study of financial markets, high-frequency trading has introduced a new era of research, yet the underlying mechanisms of such trading remain poorly understood. This paper presents a new approach to uncovering hidden patterns in trading data by applying the network motif analysis to the temporal graph model of trading activities. Our method enables the discovery of frequent and statistically significant patterns, such as "Arbitrage" and "Reinforcement" graphs, which can serve as indicators of trading strategies. These indicators are found to be more prevalent in periods of market stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the most common patterns, when applied to real-time trading data, can accurately predict changes in stock prices with a significant lead time.

The merger of a white dwarf and a black hole offers a unique opportunity to study extreme astrophysical phenomena. In a recent study, researchers simulated the collision of a white dwarf and a 10 solar mass black hole at various velocities, ranging from 0.1 to 0.8 times the speed of light. The resulting computer models indicated that the white dwarf would likely disintegrate into a disk and a surrounding atmosphere. The subsequent simulations of this system showed that the surrounding atmosphere would then fall into the black hole, causing intense X-ray emissions. The models indicated that these emissions would be most pronounced at lower velocities below 0.5 times the speed of light, and would be characterized by a prolonged 10-30 day X-ray flare. The models also suggested that the disk would be stabilized by magnetic forces, preventing it from dissipating in the environment surrounding the black hole.

To calculate three-body semileptonic $\tau$ decays including baryons, we use a chiral effective field theory at next-to-leading order. Baryon loops are considered at the leading order. Our results show significant differences between various baryonic currents and form factors, particularly when compared to those involving mesons only. The presence of baryon loops also affects the decay widths of semileptonic $\tau$ decays, such as $\tau \to 3\pi K$ and $\tau \to K K \pi$, which could be verified experimentally.

We establish a family of parametric distances that includes the Tversky measure, where the Jaccard distance is achieved when the parameter is set to 0.5, and a new distance, $\delta_{IN}$, is obtained when the parameter approaches 1. The behavior of the normalized information distance, $\delta_{N}$, as a function of set similarity is also examined, and it is found that the two distances, $\delta_{IN}$ and $\delta_{N}$, converge asymptotically.

A novel approach to movement deblurring in both human and scene images involves leveraging a generator network that mimics blur based on image content. This method is efficient and scalable, allowing it to be applied to various types of images without modification. Unlike existing methods, our approach doesn't require separate models for human and scene deblurring. Instead, a single model is trained using a mixed dataset of blurry human and scene images. In experiments, our method demonstrated superior performance on human deblurring tasks compared to state-of-the-art techniques and a comparable performance to state-of-the-art models in scene deblurring tasks.

Synthetic molecular networks have the potential to replicate complex biological systems, but their potential to mimic intricate neural behaviors is still largely unknown. We investigate the feasibility of replicating a basic learning spiking neuron, a fundamental component of artificial neural networks, using molecular reaction networks. Our study reveals that a basic learning spiking neuron, characterized by its ability to integrate synaptic inputs over time and make decisions based on those inputs, can be successfully replicated using both chemical and biological reaction networks. Additionally, we explore the impact of key parameters that influence the stability and accuracy of learning in these molecular networks, and find that their effects are comparable to those seen in biological systems.

Building on previous work by W. Marek and J. Szentmiklosi, this paper explores the concept of completeness in ultrapowers of ordered sets, specifically examining the relationship between the completeness of the ultrapower and the properties of the original ordered set. We introduce a new concept, $\mathcal{P}$-arranged sets, which satisfy a specific condition involving countable sequences of subsets, and demonstrate that the ultrapower of any $\mathcal{P}$-arranged set is complete. A fundamental theorem reveals that any ordered set, whose ultrapower is complete, can be derived from a $\mathcal{P}$-arranged set, and this result enables the proof of a previously conjectured theorem by Marek and Szentmiklosi.

Deep learning model training is now a common activity, but the process can be
involving due to the large size of datasets. To streamline this process, a
pre-training step is often used to reduce the time required for model
training. However, current pre-training methods are not tailored to specific
datasets and are instead based on general characteristics. To improve this process,
we propose a new method that involves analyzing datasets on an individual basis
to optimize the pre-training step. This method involves identifying key factors
that affect model convergence and creating a customized pre-training routine
based on these factors. Our research shows that this method can lead to a
substantial reduction in model training time, often by 50% or more, when
compared to traditional methods.

Hadwiger's Coloring Conjecture suggests that any graph with n vertices that is colored with n+1 colors must contain a complete subgraph of size n/2. This has been confirmed for networks of 4 and 5 colors, but the validity for higher colorings remains uncertain.

This research introduces an advanced adaptive algorithm for smoothly restoring graph signals, based on a generalized correntropy criterion that incorporates kernel functions. The proposed method optimizes kernel width, further enhancing its effectiveness. The study also establishes the consistency of the proposed criterion and its subgradient, along with a reliable gradient for the optimized kernel width. The framework's reliability is demonstrated through the derivation of the proposed criterion's gradient and kernel width's gradient. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on simulated data and real-world applications, showcasing its superiority over existing approaches.

We introduce a novel hybrid spinor interferometer that produces customized spin states with up to three-fold entanglement, enabling the generation of complex quantum states that go beyond the capabilities of traditional Mach-Zehnder interferometers. The entanglement of the spinor field results in an enhanced capacity for interference that surpasses detection noise, leading to a significant increase in signal-to-noise ratio of up to 9 dB. The proposed setup is highly versatile and can be applied to various atomic and photonic systems, as well as other fields like acoustics and fly-by laser ranging.
We provide a precise estimate for the first Robin eigenvalue of a nonlinear elliptic operator, specifically the fractional Laplacian, applied to a function in a bounded domain with smooth boundary.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) are a type of neural network designed to operate directly on graph data, and their success in various applications depends on their ability to extract relevant information from graph structures. However, the underlying principles of GCNNs remain unclear, particularly in how they utilize graph filters to extract meaningful features. To address this, we introduce an intuitive methodology based on matched filtering that demonstrates the feature extraction process in GCNNs. Using this approach, we visually illustrate the role of graph filters and its connection to GCNNs, thereby providing a more comprehensive understanding of these networks.

This paper introduces a novel deep contextualized auto-training method for low-resource dependency parsing. The core idea is to utilize a dependency parser trained on a high-resource language as a regulator to help a low-resource language parser learn. The regulator and the student are connected through a shared neural framework, with the regulator providing contextualized dependency labels to guide the student's learning. The regulator's contextualization module is then fine-tuned to become an auxiliary predictor for the low-resource language, effectively transferring its knowledge to the student. The paper demonstrates the method's efficacy on 8 languages with limited data and 9 languages with abundant data, achieving notable improvements on UAS and LAS metrics with the regulator's contextualization significantly enhancing the low-resource language parser's performance.

In this study, the transition form factors for $B\to D\ell\nu_\ell$ (with $\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) are examined using the self-consistent light-front quark model with a light-front Hamiltonian derived from the Bethe-Salpeter amplitude. The calculated results are presented for all four form factors ($F_1(x)$, $F_2(x)$, $G_1(z)$, $G_2(z)$) and are compared with the standard light-front quark model for the $B\to D$ transition form factors. The study also provides predictions for the $B\to D$ transition form factors and the $B\to D$ semileptonic decay branching ratios.

We investigate a type of symmetry known as non-reversible or "Galilean" symmetry in two-dimensional relativistic quantum systems. The non-reversible symmetry is a non-trivial, non-reducible extension of the established Galilean symmetry. The presence of this symmetry significantly affects the behavior of any associated topological orders. Specifically, we demonstrate that the emergent double copies of any 2D CFT that exhibits the non-reversible symmetry will have two separate copies of the original CFT. Furthermore, we show that the non-reversible symmetry leads to the doubling of any topological order found in the original CFT, resulting in a new, distinct topological order. The non-reversible symmetry also gives rise to a novel class of "membranes" that are associated with it, which we define as any 1-dimensional defect that is invariant under the non-reversible symmetry. The non-reversible symmetry is a key characteristic of the system's hidden charges, which are a fundamental aspect of the system's algebra.

In the realm of fixed-point logic, we demonstrate that a specific class of graphs can be defined by a particular acyclic program, and show that a distinct class of graphs, characterized by a different logic, can be represented by a different acyclic program, while proving that these programs have a significant property – they can be defined by a universal Turing machine in polynomial time without any restrictions.

We investigated the electronic and orbital characteristics of (Eu1-xBix)2Ir2O7 using hard X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, revealing that the material exhibits a metal-insulator transition as x increases from 0 to 1. The transition was found to occur at Bi content around 0.2< x < 0.3. The results showed that the material's electronic structure undergoes significant changes near the Fermi level as x increases, while the position of the Ir 4f core-level peak shifts towards higher binding energies. The material's electronic configuration was found to change from a 4f6 5d5 configuration in Eu2+ to a 4f3 5d1 configuration in Bi3+, indicating that Bi doping leads to increased electron count and reduced spin-orbit interactions.

This study introduces a key concept, denoted as $\mathcal{L}^p_\mathcal{K}$, to describe the properties of set-valued mappings with Lipschitz properties in a 2D space. The $L^p_\mathcal{K}$ concept is derived from this idea and is used to establish a uniform framework for studying Lipschitz selections of set-valued mappings with low dimensional sets. The paper demonstrates the existence of Lipschitz selections under this $\mathcal{L}^p_\mathcal{K}$ standard with minimal assumptions on the mapping's graph. Furthermore, the study provides efficient methods for constructing Lipschitz selections, including a direct approach and a method utilizing Bregman distance-based techniques.

The concept of a circular probability space is defined as the combination of a probability space and a free action by a finite cyclic group, resulting in an order isomorphism between its lattice of subspaces and the lattice of partitions of a set. This leads to the definition of a nontransitive probability space, which is essentially a circular probability space with a specific group action. The study of circular and nontransitive probabilities involves examining their unique characteristics and properties.

The initial setup process in a virtualized environment can be a time-consuming and resource-intensive endeavor. A novel approach, known as pre-emptive setup, enables the compile-time evaluation of setup requirements, thereby significantly reducing the time needed for the setup process. An empirical study was conducted to investigate the potential of pre-emptive setup by examining the following research questions: How can the setup process be optimized at compile-time? What are the costs associated with partial setup pre-emption? What are the factors influencing the effectiveness of pre-emptive setup? An experiment was designed to analyze the trade-offs between compile-time and run-time setup times, and the results showed that pre-emptive setup can lead to substantial compile-time setup time savings, but may also result in increased run-time configuration times.

Light dark matter particles, particularly those weighing less than a GeV, offer an attractive solution to long-standing nuclear physics issues. However, they face significant obstacles in being directly detected due to the lack of an identifiable final state and the limitations of current detection methods. This research proposes an innovative approach to overcome these challenges by utilizing electronic recoils from dark matter interactions in a reliable and dark matter-dense environment. The model involves a large water-filled tank placed underground, where electrons resulting from dark matter collisions are detected through a 10 MeV - 20 MeV energy range using a permafrost-based scintillator. This setup enables the direct detection of a 100 MeV - 1 GeV dark matter particle with a 10^-15 pb sensitivity, a range that includes previously considered models.
